problem_type: Status readability uses obsolete viewport state
symptom: Real 60 percent canvas shows 8.4 pixel status text. Composer and floating toolbar also shrink to unreadable controls.
direct_cause: Status reads legacy canvasZoom which React Flow no longer updates.
class_root: Screen-size feedback must derive from the active category viewport owner.
affected_population: Image and video feedback at reduced canvas zoom
internal_only_reason: Existing internal category viewport ownership; no new framework API.
invariants: Status compensation follows the current category viewport.
generality_proof: Both image and video nodes render NodeGenerationStatus.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Derive feedback scale from current category viewport.
Keep toolbar controls at screen size.
Derive composer size and position from current viewport.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Lab seeds the same authoritative category viewport instead of obsolete canvasZoom.

recurrence.reason: Every real zoom can reproduce this.
same_class_scan: Checked image/video status and lab viewport seeding.
Inspected GenerationCanvasReactFlowViewport onMoveEnd category viewport writeback.
NodeFloatingToolbar and useComposerViewportPlacement have the same obsolete zoom subscription; all three now consume categoryViewports.

prevention.invariant: Status compensation consumes the viewport owner.
prevention.failure_mode: Uninitialized category uses canonical initial zoom 1.
prevention.strategy: Remove legacy zoom read at shared image/video feedback renderer.

legacy_paths.rationale: Obsolete canvasZoom read removed from status.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Uses existing internal viewport store, no framework change.

residual_risks: Compensation updates at viewport gesture completion, following existing category persistence.

invariant_owner_layer.note: Real DOM screen font size measured after actual canvas zoom.
